description: A silver-grey, aromatic evergreen shrub, here mostly knee- to waist-high, with a short, gnarled, shreddy-barked trunk and small wedge-shaped leaves with three teeth at the tip, covered in fine grey hairs. It covers the dry flats and open slopes east of the crest and reaches the high benches and meadow margins of the Yosemite high country, about 1800-3200 m, where its sharp, clean smell after rain is the smell of the east side.

season_notes.winter: Evergreen and grey above the snow, the winter browse of the mule deer on the east side.
season_notes.spring: New, larger leaves flush silvery-green; the smell is strongest after rain.
season_notes.summer: Flowering stalks rise above the leaves and flatten the crown's top.
season_notes.fall: Tiny yellowish flower heads, August-October, shed clouds of pollen; then small seeds blow out across the snow.

albedo_calibration.from: 2026-11-06, calibration step (client/src/shrubfield.js fhSeason; Lamar utm12n_557_4964, June 10:00): the judged colours scaled so that, through the viewer's light, exposure and ACES (the probe judge's fair transform inverted), a full-sage canopy seen from above (a 30 m nadir view over a block of 35 % sage cover; the crowns' contribution over the block's own ground, divided by the cover) is Sentinel-2's: L2A June regressed on canopy.png shrub cover over 64k open 30 m cells gives 0.088/0.080/0.061 at full cover (grass 0.076/0.081/0.054); the twig crowns render 0.086/0.087/0.066 at k 1 and 0.080/0.081/0.061 at k 0.8 (luminance 0.0805 against 0.0803). One factor for all three channels: the satellite's redder full-cover pixel holds the bark, dead wood and litter under the crowns, not only the leaves. The eye-height check against a photograph of sunlit sage is still to be measured.

notes: Coyote brush (the template) is the nearest rounded, small-leaved evergreen shrub in the library, but sagebrush is grey, not green, with a stouter trunk (FEIS: relatively thick trunks, often one main stem), shreddy bark and a flatter, more irregular top from the flowering stalks that stand above the leaves (FEIS). In the high country of these tiles it is mainly mountain big sagebrush (subsp. vaseyana: FEIS gives 1800-3000 m in California, cool moist sites); basin big sagebrush (subsp. tridentata) is taller and lower down. FEIS lists cover for sage grouse, pygmy rabbits, small mammals and songbirds (none of the first two in the library), and winter use by mule deer; jackrabbit and fence lizard are the drafter's library stand-ins (black-tailed jackrabbits do live on the sage flats; the sagebrush lizard is the true lizard of the sage). The template's white fall flower clusters become sagebrush's small yellowish heads.
